description: Jordan is holding their late grandfather's remaining woodworking tools and must decide which family member will receive each item, where the largest tool will be kept, and how the handoff will happen after checking in with Mina and Caleb.

shared_context.S1: The family is keeping three of their grandfather's workshop items: a benchtop planer, a scroll saw, and a locked chest of hand tools.
shared_context.S2: Jordan is storing the items temporarily and will make the final decisions about who receives each one.
shared_context.S3: The family wants the items to remain with relatives rather than being sold.
shared_context.S4: The planer is too large for ordinary car transport and needs a secure, level place to be kept.
shared_context.S5: Jordan's usual family check-in is to ask Mina and Caleb in turn about their plans, available space, and any practical details before settling the arrangement; each person confirms their own details as part of that check-in.
shared_context.S6: After hearing both relatives, Jordan summarizes the reasons for the assignments and explains the handoff plan before making the final call.
shared_context.S7: Jordan's workshop handoff checklist includes the recipient, the item's exact destination, and a pickup plan for each item.
shared_context.S8: For bulky equipment, Jordan arranges a two-person carry and confirms that the destination is ready before the handoff.
shared_context.S9: During the family check-in, each person describes any project, space, measurement, or practical detail that should be considered, and Jordan records the person's confirmed details before moving to the next person.
shared_context.S10: Jordan does not finalize the arrangement until both relatives have completed their check-in, and the final summary records the specific plans and practical details that support each assignment or handoff.
shared_context.S11: Jordan's family handoff routine requires each relative to formally confirm any project or destination detail they want used, and Jordan's final summary credits every relative whose confirmed detail shaped an assignment.

PF1.text: Mina has promised to use the planer to build an accessibility ramp for their aunt, and her garage has a clear 120-centimeter west bench beside a 240-volt outlet; she has not yet told Jordan.

PF2.text: Caleb is restoring the unfinished birdhouse their grandfather started and specifically needs the grandfather's scroll saw for that project; he has a dry 90-centimeter shelf where it can remain set up, but he has not yet told Jordan.

decisions.planer_storage: string; use 'Mina_west_bench_120cm_240V_garage' for Mina's specified garage setup
decisions.scroll_saw_storage: string; use 'Caleb_dry_shelf_90cm' for Caleb's specified shelf

acceptance_conditions: Mina must receive the benchtop planer.
The planer must be kept on Mina's 120-centimeter west garage bench beside the 240-volt outlet.
Caleb must receive the scroll saw.
The scroll saw must be placed on Caleb's dry 90-centimeter shelf.
A pickup-plan commitment must record Mina's planer handoff to the specified west bench and 240-volt outlet.
A pickup-plan commitment must record Caleb's scroll-saw placement on the specified 90-centimeter shelf for the birdhouse restoration.
Mina's planer plan and Caleb's birdhouse project must each be cited as justification for their assignments.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'pickup_plan' and c['target'] == 'planer' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'pickup_plan' and c['target'] == 'scroll_saw' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Mina's accessibility-ramp promise changes the planer recipient to Mina, while her exact 120-centimeter west bench and 240-volt outlet change the storage value and required pickup-plan detail.
Caleb's unfinished birdhouse project changes the scroll saw recipient to Caleb, while his exact dry 90-centimeter shelf changes the required storage and pickup-plan detail.
